A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RBD research, with matching methods and substantial retained experimental content. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original bias-detection training results, evaluations across eight LLM evaluators, ablations, generalization tests, and latency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds external-benchmark evaluations, prompt ablations, and expanded latency measurements.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same teacher-supervised reasoning training, bias detection, and iterative evaluator correction. The new prompt experiments and serving configuration do not revise the proposed RBD algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluations using LLMBar and JudgeBench response pairs for verbosity and bandwagon bias (Section 5.4). These extend coverage beyond the retained constructed datasets, including cases where longer answers or majority-endorsed answers can be either correct or incorrect.

E2.justification: The prompting baselines, zero-shot DeepSeek-R1, label-only fine-tuning, Prometheus2-8×7B, and Skywork-LLaMA-3.1-70B are retained. The label-only comparison moves from the appendix into the main text; external benchmarks reuse existing evaluator and RBD configurations.

E3.justification: New protocols select external pairs with length differences exceeding 150 tokens and randomly assign majority endorsements, with sample sizes specified in Appendix C.7. Prompt-ablation conditions are added. Main latency reporting changes from batch size 1 to vLLM at batch size 4; existing training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.6 adds controlled tests of dependence on evaluator identity and knowledge of the specific bias type. Appendix C.10 adds latency comparisons across model sizes and serving implementations. The diagnostic-set, multi-bias, cross-domain, and iterative-refinement analyses already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose training seed 3407. Neither introduces repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; the added experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds external-benchmark and prompt-ablation results. For example, Table 3 reports average verbosity accuracy of 0.681 versus 0.792 with RBD-14B on LLMBar. Reported latency changes from 6.6 to 1.5 seconds under different serving settings. Retained benchmark scores and plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The bias-label definition, training objective, accuracy and consistency formulas, and stubbornness and overconfidence definitions remain unchanged. The latter move from Appendix C.7 to C.8; no new theoretical results or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about modular debiasing, scalability, generalization, and efficiency, including the headline improvements. New experiments supply additional support without redefining those core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets prompt ablations as evidence that explicit evaluator identity and specific bias labels are unnecessary. Section 6 additionally suggests that behavioral biases can persist or intensify through distillation and compression. Appendix F's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the evaluator reevaluation prompt in Appendix E.5, a worked interaction in D.3, and additional prompt and serving details. These expand documentation of the existing pipeline. Training hyperparameters, hardware, and the code/data access statement are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for vLLM/PagedAttention and LLMBar. JudgeBench was already cited in v1. The related-work discussion and positioning of RBD relative to prompting and fine-tuned judges otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 creates a dedicated generalization subsection, promotes the existing label-only diagnostic discussion into Section 5.2, and moves iterative refinement into Appendix C.9. It also adds explanatory examples and makes localized wording edits while retaining the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds external-benchmark, prompt-ablation, and detailed latency tables, reformats evaluation-table headers and improvement annotations, and relocates existing plots between the main text and appendix. The underlying plotted graphics are retained rather than redrawn with new results.

improvement.justification: External-benchmark tests and prompt ablations strengthen evidence beyond v1's constructed evaluations, while the explicit reevaluation prompt improves reproducibility. The gains are tempered by reporting defects: Section 5.4 reverses the dataset order associated with Table 3's averages, and Appendix D.3 contains option labels and an outcome inconsistent with its quoted reasoning and retained Figure 11. The added evidence supports a limited overall improvement despite these clarity problems.
